```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggthemes)
  library(ggridges)
  library(gt)
  library(knitr)
  library(tibble)
  library(purrr)
})

theme_set(ggthemes::theme_few())

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) y else x

# Render can run with working dir = reporting/, so climb one level if needed.
wd <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
rtmb_root <- if (file.exists(file.path(wd, "R", "Rpm.R"))) wd else normalizePath(file.path(wd, ".."), mustWork = TRUE)
rtmb_file <- function(...) normalizePath(file.path(rtmb_root, ...), mustWork = FALSE)

results_dir <- rtmb_file(params$results_dir)

run_path <- function(form) file.path(results_dir, sprintf("fishery_sel_form_%d.rds", as.integer(form)))

load_run <- function(form) {
  path <- if (as.integer(form) == 2L) {
    local_path <- file.path(
      rtmb_root, "analysis", "output", "double_logistic_experiments",
      "cv0p2_no_old_age_cap_stage2_random.rds"
    )
    legacy_path <- file.path(
      dirname(rtmb_root), "rtmb_ebswp_form2", "analysis", "output",
      "double_logistic_experiments", "cv0p2_no_old_age_cap_stage2_random.rds"
    )
    if (file.exists(local_path)) local_path else legacy_path
  } else {
    run_path(form)
  }
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing results file: ", path)
  x <- readRDS(path)
  if (as.integer(form) == 2L) {
    x$form <- 2L
    x$label <- "Time-age varying double logistic (20% CV)"
    x$fixed_parameters <- x$fitted_parameters
  }
  x$path <- path
  x
}

base_form <- as.integer(params$base_form)
compare_forms <- as.integer(params$compare_forms)
forms <- c(base_form, compare_forms)
runs <- purrr::map(forms, load_run)

safe_logit_rho <- function(x) 2 / (1 + exp(-x)) - 1

# Short labels for plotting (full labels can get clipped in facets)
short_label <- function(form) {
  form <- as.integer(form)
  if (form == 0L) return("Base")
  if (form == 2L) return("Double-logistic (20% CV)")
  if (form == 5L) return("2D AR1")
  paste0("Form ", form)
}

summary_tbl <- tibble(
  fishery_sel_form = purrr::map_int(runs, "form"),
  label = purrr::map_chr(runs, "label"),
  label_short = purrr::map_chr(purrr::map_int(runs, "form"), short_label),
  objective = purrr::map_dbl(runs, "objective"),
  evaluated_total = purrr::map_dbl(runs, ~ .x$evaluated_total %||% .x$report$tot_like %||% NA_real_),
  n_parameters = purrr::map_int(
    runs,
    ~ as.integer(.x$n_parameters %||% length(.x$fit$par) %||% NA_integer_)
  ),
  n_random = purrr::map_int(runs, ~ if (isTRUE(.x$random_effects)) {
    length(.x$fitted_parameters$sel_double_logistic_dev_fsh %||% numeric())
  } else 0L),
  convergence = purrr::map_int(runs, "convergence"),
  max_gradient = purrr::map_dbl(runs, "max_gradient"),
  seconds = purrr::map_dbl(runs, "seconds")
) |>
  arrange(fishery_sel_form) |>
  mutate(
    # The form-2 objective is Laplace marginal; fixed-effect objectives are joint.
    # Do not present their difference as a like-for-like model comparison.
    delta_objective = if_else(
      fishery_sel_form == 2L, NA_real_,
      objective - objective[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1]
    ),
    delta_evaluated_total = if_else(
      fishery_sel_form == 2L, NA_real_,
      evaluated_total - evaluated_total[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1]
    ),
    objective_report_gap = if_else(
      fishery_sel_form == 2L, NA_real_, evaluated_total - objective
    )
  )

rho_ar1_summary <- {
  ar1_run <- runs[[which(purrr::map_int(runs, "form") == 5L)[1]]]
  rho_working <- ar1_run$fixed_parameters$sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh %||% c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
  rho <- safe_logit_rho(as.numeric(rho_working))
  tibble(
    fishery_sel_form = 5L,
    label_short = short_label(5L),
    rho_y = rho[1],
    rho_a = rho[2],
    working_rho_y = as.numeric(rho_working[1]),
    working_rho_a = as.numeric(rho_working[2])
  )
}

rho_ar1_caption <- if (nrow(rho_ar1_summary) > 0 && all(is.finite(rho_ar1_summary$rho_y), is.finite(rho_ar1_summary$rho_a))) {
  sprintf(
    " For the 2D AR1 form, fitted correlations are rho_y = %.3f and rho_a = %.3f.",
    rho_ar1_summary$rho_y,
    rho_ar1_summary$rho_a
  )
} else {
  ""
}

get_ssb_df <- function(run) {
  ssb <- run$report$SSB
  tibble(
    fishery_sel_form = run$form,
    label = run$label,
    label_short = short_label(run$form),
    year = as.integer(names(ssb)),
    SSB = as.numeric(ssb)
  )
}

# Note: fishery selectivity is stored as sel_fsh in the report list (matrix [year x age])
get_sel_df <- function(run) {
  sel <- run$report$sel_fsh
  stopifnot(is.matrix(sel))
  years <- as.integer(rownames(sel) %||% seq_len(nrow(sel)))
  if (is.null(rownames(sel))) years <- seq_len(nrow(sel))
  out <- as_tibble(sel, .name_repair = "minimal")
  names(out) <- seq_len(ncol(sel))
  out |>
    mutate(year = years, .before = 1) |>
    pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "age", values_to = "selectivity") |>
    mutate(
      age = as.integer(age),
      fishery_sel_form = run$form,
      label = run$label,
      label_short = short_label(run$form)
    )
}

ssb_df <- bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, get_ssb_df))
sel_df <- bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, get_sel_df))

get_catch_df <- function(run) {
  obs <- run$report$obs_catch
  pred <- run$report$pred_catch
  yrs <- as.integer(names(obs) %||% names(pred) %||% seq_along(obs))
  tibble(
    fishery_sel_form = run$form,
    label = run$label,
    label_short = short_label(run$form),
    year = yrs,
    obs_catch = as.numeric(obs),
    pred_catch = as.numeric(pred)
  )
}

catch_df <- bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, get_catch_df))

# Generic GT wrapper

gt_report <- function(data, ...) {
  gt(data, ...) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
}

plot_agecomp_fit_comparison <- function(data, fleet_name, ncol = 4) {
  plot_data <- data |>
    filter(fleet == fleet_name, is.finite(obs) | is.finite(exp)) |>
    mutate(label_short = factor(label_short, levels = unique(summary_tbl$label_short)))

  observed_data <- plot_data |>
    group_by(fleet, year, age) |>
    summarize(obs = mean(obs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot() +
    geom_line(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(x = age, y = exp, color = label_short, group = label_short),
      linewidth = 0.5,
      alpha = 0.9,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = observed_data,
      aes(x = age, y = obs),
      color = "#1f78b4",
      size = 0.85,
      alpha = 0.75,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~year, ncol = ncol, dir = "v") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
    labs(
      x = "Age",
      y = "Proportion",
      color = "Scenario",
      title = paste(fleet_name, "Age Composition Fits")
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

# Purpose

::: {.selectivity-hero}
::: {.selectivity-intro}
This is the single selectivity page for the RTMB EBS pollock project. It
combines the description of implemented selectivity forms, fitted scenario
results, diagnostic comparisons, assessment effects, and implementation
references that were previously split among three pages.

[Return to the EBS pollock assessment](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/EBS_pollock_stock_assessment/){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

::: {.selectivity-logo}
<a href="https://afsc-assessments.github.io/EBS_pollock_stock_assessment/" aria-label="EBS pollock assessment home">
  <img src="../assets/logo2.png" alt="Walleye pollock illustration with NOAA Fisheries identification">
</a>
:::
:::

This report compares three RTMB runs that differ **only** in the fishery selectivity form.

- Base: `fishery_sel_form = ` `r params$base_form`
- Comparators: `fishery_sel_form = ` `r paste(params$compare_forms, collapse = ", ")`

The base and 2D AR1 outputs were generated by
`R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R`. The time-age varying double-logistic
output was generated by `R/run_double_logistic_experiments.R` in the isolated
`rtmb_ebswp_form2` worktree. Results are loaded from:

- `r params$results_dir` (base and 2D AR1)
- `analysis/output/double_logistic_experiments/` (stage-2 double logistic)

::: {.callout-important title="How to use this page"}
Optimization and likelihood results should be considered together with
age-composition fits, selectivity patterns, spawning biomass, convergence,
and biological plausibility. A lower objective value alone is insufficient to
select an assessment configuration.
:::

## Forms included

| Form | Implementation | Time variation | Role in this report |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0: Base coefficients | Estimated log-selectivity coefficients by age | Deviations at configured change years | Bridge-compatible reference and current base form |
| 2: Time-age varying double logistic | Ascending and descending logistic limbs | Annual random deviations around a shared mean curve, with fixed 20% process CV | Parsimonious dome-shaped sensitivity with substantial interannual change |
| 5: 2D AR1 | Latent log-selectivity surface over year and age | Separable AR1 correlation across neighboring years and ages | Flexible time-varying sensitivity |

The fishery forms are the focus of the fitted comparison. The model also uses
fleet-specific selectivity structures for BTS and ATS; the relevant code and
parameter mapping are summarized in the implementation appendix.

# Fit Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Model optimization summary by fishery selectivity form. Fixed parameters is the number supplied to nlminb; random effects is the number integrated by the Laplace approximation. For forms 0 and 5, the optimizer and reported totals are joint NLL values and delta columns are differences from form 0. For form 2, the optimizer objective is marginal while the reported total is conditional joint NLL, so cross-form deltas and the report-minus-optimizer gap are not shown. Convergence 0 indicates normal nlminb completion."
summary_tbl |>
  select(
    fishery_sel_form, label_short, n_parameters, n_random, objective, evaluated_total,
    delta_objective, delta_evaluated_total, objective_report_gap,
    convergence, max_gradient, seconds
  ) |>
  gt_report() |>
  tab_header(title = "Fit summary") |>
  cols_label(
    fishery_sel_form = "Form",
    label_short = "Scenario",
    n_parameters = "Fixed parameters",
    n_random = "Random effects",
    objective = "Optimizer objective",
    evaluated_total = "Reported total NLL",
    delta_objective = "Delta objective",
    delta_evaluated_total = "Delta reported NLL",
    objective_report_gap = "Report - optimizer gap",
    convergence = "Convergence",
    max_gradient = "Maximum gradient",
    seconds = "Seconds"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      objective, evaluated_total, delta_objective,
      delta_evaluated_total, objective_report_gap
    ),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = seconds, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = max_gradient, decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(n_parameters, n_random, convergence))
```

The **Report - optimizer gap** is an internal consistency check. A substantial
gap indicates that the optimizer and the saved report were evaluated with
different data, parameter values, model switches, or likelihood bookkeeping.
It should not be interpreted as an improvement in model fit. The gap should be
near zero for the fixed-effect fits. It is not shown for the time-age varying
double logistic because its optimized objective is the Laplace marginal
objective, whereas the reported total is the joint objective evaluated at the
fitted random-effect modes. Those quantities have different definitions, so
their difference would not indicate a reporting mismatch.

```{r}
#| label: objective-report-gap-warning
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

gap_max <- max(abs(summary_tbl$objective_report_gap), na.rm = TRUE)
if (is.finite(gap_max) && gap_max > 1e-3) {
  cat(
    "\n\n> **Diagnostic warning:** at least one saved run has a large ",
    "`objective_report_gap`. Regenerate the scenario `.rds` files with the ",
    "current `R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R` before interpreting the ",
    "selectivity comparison.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

# Likelihood Component Comparison

## Age-composition fit comparison

The model returns an age-composition negative log-likelihood contribution by fleet in `report$age_like`.

It also stores fishery observed (`oac_fsh`) and expected (`eac_fsh`) age-composition proportions by year×age in the saved run outputs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-like
#| fig-cap: "Change in age-composition NLL relative to the base scenario by fleet. Form 2 is the hierarchical double logistic with 20% process CV. These conditional fleet-specific likelihood contributions are comparable as data-fit diagnostics because they use the same observations and likelihood, but they are not marginal overall model objectives. Negative values indicate improved fit relative to base."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: "100%"

age_like_df <- bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, function(run) {
  al <- run$report$age_like
  tibble(
    fishery_sel_form = run$form,
    label = run$label,
    label_short = short_label(run$form),
    fleet = names(al),
    age_like = as.numeric(al)
  )
})) |>
  mutate(
    fleet = factor(fleet, levels = c("fsh", "bts", "ats"), labels = c("Fishery", "BTS", "ATS")),
    label = factor(label, levels = unique(summary_tbl$label)),
    label_short = factor(label_short, levels = unique(summary_tbl$label_short))
  )

base_vals <- age_like_df |>
  filter(fishery_sel_form == base_form) |>
  select(fleet, base_age_like = age_like)

age_like_df2 <- age_like_df |>
  left_join(base_vals, by = "fleet") |>
  mutate(delta_age_like = age_like - base_age_like)

age_like_plot_df <- age_like_df2 |>
  filter(fishery_sel_form != base_form)

ggplot(age_like_plot_df, aes(x = label_short, y = delta_age_like, fill = label_short)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "gray50") +
  geom_col(width = 0.68, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = round(delta_age_like, 1),
      vjust = ifelse(delta_age_like >= 0, -0.35, 1.25)
    ),
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~fleet, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Delta age-comp NLL vs base", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-age-like
#| tbl-cap: "Age-composition NLL contributions (and deltas vs base) by fleet and scenario."

age_like_df2 |>
  mutate(across(c(age_like, base_age_like, delta_age_like), ~round(.x, 0))) |>
  arrange(fleet, fishery_sel_form) |>
  gt_report()
```

## One-step-ahead residual comparison {#sec-osa-comparison}

One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals provide a distribution-based check of the age-composition fits. The comparison uses the updated local `afscOSA` package, multinomial residuals, the same observed compositions and effective sample sizes for every approach, and seed 202508. Each gear has one figure, with one column per fitted selectivity approach: base coefficients, the time-age varying double logistic with 20% process CV, and the 2D AR1 surface. The stage-1 shared curve was only an initialization step and is not treated as a competing assessment configuration.

The acoustic-trawl survey calculation uses ages 2--15. Its 2020 composition is omitted because restricting the data to those ages produces zero rounded observations; this rule is applied identically to all three approaches. As in the standard `afscOSA` plotting method, residuals outside +/-6 are capped in the figures only so the main patterns remain visible; their uncapped finite values are retained in the summary table.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-osa-summary
#| tbl-cap: "OSA residual summaries by gear and selectivity approach. SDNR is the standard deviation of the OSA residuals; values near 1 are consistent with the assumed residual scale. The last two columns give the percentage of absolute residuals exceeding 2 and 3."

osa_summary <- readr::read_csv(
  rtmb_file(
    "analysis", "output", "osa_selectivity_comparison",
    "osa_selectivity_summary.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  transmute(
    Gear = recode(gear, fishery = "Fishery", bts = "BTS", ats = "ATS"),
    Approach = approach,
    `Number of residuals` = n_residuals,
    SDNR = round(sdnr, 2),
    `Mean residual` = round(mean, 2),
    `|residual| > 2 (%)` = round(100 * proportion_abs_gt_2, 1),
    `|residual| > 3 (%)` = round(100 * proportion_abs_gt_3, 1)
  )

osa_summary |>
  gt_report()
```

The fishery comparison is the clearest separation among methods (@fig-osa-fishery). The time-age varying double logistic has SDNR 1.26 and 11.0% of residuals outside +/-2, while the base and 2D AR1 approaches remain closer to the reference scale (SDNR 0.88 and 0.84). Differences are smaller for BTS (@fig-osa-bts), while all three approaches give similar ATS residual distributions (@fig-osa-ats). The 20% process CV materially improves the double-logistic residuals but does not remove all aggregate structure. These diagnostics favor the more flexible fishery selectivity forms; they do not by themselves establish which configuration should be used for assessment.

## Age Composition Fits

These figures follow the observed-versus-expected age-composition layout used for figures 5-7 in the main assessment report. Points show the observed proportions; colored lines show the expected proportions from each fishery selectivity scenario.

```{r}
#| label: agecomp-data
#| include: false

extract_agecomp_df <- function(run, fleet = c("fsh", "bts", "ats")) {
  fleet <- match.arg(fleet)

  # Observations and their years are common to every scenario. Some compact
  # Stage 2 checkpoints retain predictions but omit duplicated input arrays.
  reference_report <- runs[[which(vapply(
    runs,
    function(x) !is.null(x$report[[paste0("oac_", fleet)]]),
    logical(1)
  ))[1]]]$report
  oac <- run$report[[paste0("oac_", fleet)]] %||%
    reference_report[[paste0("oac_", fleet)]]
  eac <- run$report[[paste0("phat_", fleet)]]
  stopifnot(!is.null(oac), !is.null(eac))

  yrs_key <- paste0("yrs_", fleet, "_data")
  yrs <- run$report[[yrs_key]] %||% reference_report[[yrs_key]]
  if (is.null(yrs) || length(yrs) != nrow(oac)) {
    # Fallback if years weren't saved (shouldn't happen): use row index
    yrs <- seq_len(nrow(oac))
  }

  sample_size <- run$report[[paste0("sam_", fleet)]] %||%
    reference_report[[paste0("sam_", fleet)]]
  if (is.null(sample_size) || length(sample_size) != nrow(oac)) {
    sample_size <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(oac))
  }

  ages <- seq_len(ncol(oac))

  # Match the main report's age-composition plots by comparing BTS/ATS over ages 2+.
  if (fleet %in% c("bts", "ats") && ncol(oac) >= 2) {
    keep <- 2:ncol(oac)
    oac <- oac[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    eac <- eac[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    ages <- keep
  }

  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(year = yrs, age = ages) |>
    as.data.frame()
  grid$fishery_sel_form <- run$form
  grid$label <- run$label
  grid$label_short <- short_label(run$form)
  grid$fleet <- fleet

  # Convert to proportions within each year-row to make diagnostics comparable.
  # Some ATS expected values are stored on an abundance scale before this normalization.
  o_rs <- pmax(rowSums(oac), 1e-12)
  e_rs <- pmax(rowSums(eac), 1e-12)
  o_prop <- sweep(oac, 1, o_rs, "/")
  e_prop <- sweep(eac, 1, e_rs, "/")

  # Safety: enforce exact renormalization numerically (and catch pathologies)
  o_prop <- sweep(o_prop, 1, pmax(rowSums(o_prop), 1e-12), "/")
  e_prop <- sweep(e_prop, 1, pmax(rowSums(e_prop), 1e-12), "/")

  # Optional checks (won't stop render, but will warn in console if something is off)
  o_chk <- max(abs(rowSums(o_prop) - 1))
  e_chk <- max(abs(rowSums(e_prop) - 1))
  if (is.finite(o_chk) && o_chk > 1e-6) warning("oac proportions do not sum to 1 (max abs dev = ", o_chk, ") for fleet=", fleet, ", form=", run$form)
  if (is.finite(e_chk) && e_chk > 1e-6) warning("eac proportions do not sum to 1 (max abs dev = ", e_chk, ") for fleet=", fleet, ", form=", run$form)

  grid$obs <- as.numeric(t(o_prop))
  grid$exp <- as.numeric(t(e_prop))
  grid$resid <- grid$obs - grid$exp
  grid$n_eff <- rep(as.numeric(sample_size), each = length(ages))

  tibble::as_tibble(grid)
}

agecomp_df <- bind_rows(
  purrr::map_dfr(runs, extract_agecomp_df, fleet = "fsh"),
  purrr::map_dfr(runs, extract_agecomp_df, fleet = "bts"),
  purrr::map_dfr(runs, extract_agecomp_df, fleet = "ats")
) |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(label, levels = unique(summary_tbl$label)),
    label_short = factor(label_short, levels = unique(summary_tbl$label_short)),
    fleet = factor(fleet, levels = c("fsh", "bts", "ats"), labels = c("Fishery", "BTS", "ATS"))
  )
```

The RTMB report object stores a set of likelihood (or penalty) components. The most relevant ones for this comparison are:

- `sel_like`, `sel_like_dev` (selectivity penalties)
- `age_like` (age composition likelihood)
- `cat_like` (catch fit)
- `cpue_like` (CPUE)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nll-components
#| tbl-cap: "Selected likelihood / penalty components returned in the RTMB report."

extract_components <- function(run) {
  r <- run$report
  tibble(
    fishery_sel_form = run$form,
    label = run$label,
    sel_like = sum(r$sel_like, na.rm = TRUE),
    sel_like_dev = sum(r$sel_like_dev, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_like_total = attr(r$age_like, "total") %||% sum(r$age_like, na.rm = TRUE),
    cat_like = r$cat_like %||% NA_real_,
    cpue_like = r$cpue_like %||% NA_real_,
    avo_like = r$avo_like %||% NA_real_,
    wt_like = r$wt_like %||% NA_real_,
    nll = r$tot_like %||% r$nll %||% NA_real_
  )
}

comp_tbl <- bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, extract_components)) |>
  arrange(fishery_sel_form) |>
  mutate(
    delta_nll = nll - nll[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1],
    delta_sel_like = sel_like - sel_like[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1],
    delta_sel_like_dev = sel_like_dev - sel_like_dev[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1]
  )

comp_tbl |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 0))) |>
  gt_report() |>
  tab_header(title = "NLL components")
```

# Fishery Selectivity Surfaces

Fishery selectivity is represented as a relative age pattern that multiplies annual fully selected fishing mortality. Let $t$ index years, $a$ index ages, and $x_a = a + 0.5$ denote the age value used in the selectivity functions. Each form is converted to log selectivity $\ell_{t,a}$, centered within year, and exponentiated. The base and 2D AR1 comparison runs constrain ages 11 and older to share the age-11 value:

$$
\ell_{t,a} = \ell_{t,11}, \quad a \ge 11,
$$

The time-age varying double logistic does not impose this equality; its
descending limb is evaluated separately through age 15.

$$
\ell^*_{t,a} =
\ell_{t,a} -
\log \left\{ A^{-1} \sum_{a=1}^{A} \exp(\ell_{t,a}) \right\},
\qquad
s_{t,a} = \exp(\ell^*_{t,a}).
$$

The centered selectivity $s_{t,a}$ enters the population dynamics as $F_{t,a} = F_t s_{t,a}$. Code references needed to reproduce the implementation are in @sec-appendix-implementation.

## Literature context

@sampson2014fishery provides a useful framing for this comparison by separating contact selection, availability, and population-level fishery selectivity. That distinction matters here because the RTMB selectivity surface is not simply a gear-retention curve; it is the relative fishing mortality pattern implied by the combined fishery, fleet behavior, fish distribution, and assessment model structure. The paper also illustrates that population selectivity can be temporally variable and can take diverse shapes, which motivates comparing the base change-year coefficient form against more flexible alternatives.

@punt2014model focuses on the assessment-model problem: selectivity forms reduce variance when they are parsimonious, but they can bias assessment outputs when the assumed functional form is wrong. The paper reviews how residual diagnostics, information criteria, and simulation studies can be used to evaluate selectivity choices. This report follows that logic by comparing model likelihood components, age-composition fits, selectivity surfaces, and spawning biomass trajectories rather than interpreting one selectivity form from the objective value alone.

@martell2014goodPractices is the most direct precedent for the time-varying selectivity comparison. Martell and Stewart used simulation-estimation experiments to evaluate fixed, blocked, and continuously changing selectivity patterns and emphasized that both statistical fit and policy consequences should be evaluated. The base model here resembles a blocked approach through change-year deviations, whereas the 2D AR1 option is closer to a continuous time-varying surface that borrows strength across neighboring years and ages.

@butterworth2014selectivityMatter asks how much selectivity uncertainty affects management advice across a set of applied assessment and management-procedure examples. The study is a caution against treating selectivity sensitivity as automatically dominant: selectivity can strongly affect reference points and biomass scale in some cases, but other uncertainties may be equally or more influential. For this report, that means SSB and likelihood differences should be read as one part of a broader sensitivity analysis rather than as a complete basis for model choice.

@cadrin2016fieldObservations connects assessment selectivity and catchability to field observations of fishing gear, survey gear, efficiency, and availability. The paper is relevant because assessment-estimated selectivity can absorb several processes that field studies may measure separately. For EBS pollock, any interpretation of the fishery selectivity surface should therefore distinguish model-based population selectivity from direct observations about gear performance, fishing behavior, or fish availability.

@vasilakopoulos2020metrics shifts the focus from estimating selectivity curves to operational metrics for management advice. The authors evaluate candidate metrics for sensitivity to selectivity changes and robustness to recruitment and fishing-mortality variation, identifying the ratio of fishing mortality on the first recruited age to average fishing mortality as a useful summary. That perspective suggests a practical extension of this comparison: after fitting alternative selectivity forms, summarize whether the implied exploitation pattern changes in a way that managers could track, not only whether the full selectivity surface looks different.

## Form 0: base coefficients with change-year deviations

The base EBS pollock form follows the statistical approach developed by
@butterworth2003sbt, which placed catch-at-age fitting in a likelihood framework
and allowed age-specific selectivity to change over time within a specified
structure. That paper is the key methodological reference for the assessment's
use of age coefficients with time-varying deviations.

The implemented base model uses estimated age coefficients plus deviations at
configured fishery-selectivity change years:

$$
\ell_{t,a} = c_a + d_{k(t),a},
$$

where $c_a$ is the baseline age coefficient and $d_{k(t),a}$ is the deviation for the change-year block $k(t)$. This form is flexible at the configured break points but does not estimate a continuous year-to-year process for fishery selectivity.

## Form 2: time-age varying double logistic

The double-logistic curve is generated from positive parameters $p_{1,t}$, $p_{2,t}$, and $p_{3,t}$. The model estimates their logarithms, so $p_{j,t}=\exp(\theta_{t,j})$. The initial values on the natural scale are 1.5, 3, and 4. These parameters define the ascending and descending transition ages:

$$
\gamma_{1,t} = p_{1,t} + p_{2,t},
\qquad
\gamma_{2,t} = 2p_{1,t} + p_{2,t} + p_{3,t}.
$$

The two logistic limbs are

$$
u_{t,a} =
\left[1 + \exp\left\{-\log(19)\frac{x_a - \gamma_{1,t}}{p_{1,t}}\right\}\right]^{-1},
$$

$$
v_{t,a} =
1 -
\left[1 + \exp\left\{-\log(19)\frac{x_a - \gamma_{2,t}}{p_{3,t}}\right\}\right]^{-1},
$$

Following the EBS pollock prior-elicitation formulation, the raw curve is

$$
s^{\mathrm{hard}}_{t,a} =
\min\left\{1,\;u_{t,a}v_{t,a}0.95^{-2}\right\}.
$$

The literal minimum has a kink where its two arguments meet. The RTMB
implementation therefore uses the differentiable approximation

$$
s_{t,a} = 1 - \frac{\log\left[1+\exp\{\kappa(1-r_{t,a})\}\right]}{\kappa}
+ \frac{\log\{1+\exp(-\kappa)\}}{\kappa},
\qquad r_{t,a}=u_{t,a}v_{t,a}0.95^{-2},\quad \kappa=50.
$$

This transform is zero at zero, approaches one smoothly, and closely follows
the hard cap except immediately around $r_{t,a}=1$. Define
$b_{t,a}=\log(s_{t,a}+\epsilon)$.

It is then centered so arithmetic mean selectivity within each year is one:

$$
\ell_{t,a} = b_{t,a} -
\log\left\{\frac{1}{A}\sum_{a'=1}^{A}\exp(b_{t,a'})\right\}.
$$

An earlier implementation subtracted $\max_a b_{t,a}$ before this centering.
That subtraction was unnecessary: centering removes any common additive
constant, so $\operatorname{center}(b-\max b)=\operatorname{center}(b)$ apart
from numerical roundoff. It was removed because `max()` is not differentiable
when the age attaining the maximum changes. The standard implementation then
sets ages 11 and older equal to the age-11 value and centers the result again;
the uncapped sensitivity below omits that equality constraint.

The original annual fixed-effect implementation estimated one log-scale triplet $\theta_t = (\log p_{1,t},\log p_{2,t},\log p_{3,t})$ for every year. It used shrinkage toward $\mu_0 = \log(1.5,3,4)$ and a first-difference penalty:

$$
Q_\mathrm{fixed} =
\sum_t \sum_j
\left(\frac{\theta_{t,j} - \mu_{0,j}}{\sigma_{p,j}}\right)^2
+
\frac{1}{2}
\sum_{t=2}^{T} \sum_j
\left(\frac{\theta_{t,j} - \theta_{t-1,j}}{\sigma_{\Delta,j}}\right)^2,
$$

where $\sigma_p = (0.75,0.75,0.45)$ and $\sigma_\Delta = (0.60,0.60,0.40)$. This is the 183-parameter formulation that failed the convergence checks; it is retained here to document that attempt, not as the formulation used for the corrected stage-2 results.

The successful staged formulation does not use the first-difference term above. Stage 1 estimates a single mean triplet $\mu$ shared across years, with

$$
Q_1 =
\sum_j
\left(\frac{\mu_j-\mu_{0,j}}{\sigma_{p,j}}\right)^2.
$$

Stage 2 defines the annual log-scale parameters as

$$
\theta_t = \mu + \delta_t,
\qquad
\delta_{t,j} \overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}
\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\mathrm{CV}}^2),
\qquad
\sigma_{\mathrm{CV}} = \sqrt{\log(1+0.20^2)} = 0.1980.
$$

Ignoring normalizing constants, the corresponding penalty is

$$
Q_2 =
\sum_j
\left(\frac{\mu_j-\mu_{0,j}}{\sigma_{p,j}}\right)^2
+
\frac{1}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{CV}}^2}
\sum_t\sum_j \delta_{t,j}^2.
$$

The code evaluates the random-effect contribution with the full normal log density and integrates the annual deviations using RTMB's Laplace approximation. The current section-2.6 implementation retains the configured across-age curvature penalty but omits the historical old-age shape penalty. The smaller prior scale for the third mean parameter provides stronger shrinkage on the descending limb, which is otherwise weakly informed by older ages.

### Testing option 2 locally {#sec-form2-local-testing}

The initial option-2 fit should be treated as a convergence diagnosis rather
than as a candidate assessment result. It estimated 61 annual parameter
triplets, or 183 double-logistic parameters. The saved run ended with optimizer
code 1 (`false convergence (8)`) and a maximum absolute gradient of 1.8366.
Its objective value was 8299.2 and agreed with the independently evaluated
reported total to numerical precision. Thus, the objective was evaluated
consistently, but the parameter estimates do not yet satisfy the convergence
standard needed for biological or assessment interpretation.

::: {.callout-important title="Result of the staged tests"}
The originally implemented annual fixed-effect option failed, but the corrected
two-stage section-2.6 formulation converged. A shared three-parameter curve was
estimated first, followed by zero-centered annual random effects with a fixed
20% CV. Stage 1 had a maximum gradient of 0.00045 and stage 2 had a marginal
gradient of 0.000068. After two unused parameters were removed, the stage-2
Hessian was positive definite and finite standard errors were obtained.
:::

The selectable-form implementation used to generate the existing comparison
is preserved at Git commit `cd46353`. The current `main` branch instead
preserves the exact September 2025 ADMB--RTMB bridge. Consequently, local
option-2 experiments should be run in a separate Git worktree based on
`cd46353`; this prevents experimental selectivity changes from altering the
validated bridge or the published site source.

#### Step 1: create an isolated experiment

From the repository containing this report:

```bash
git fetch --all --prune
git worktree add \
  -b experiment/double-logistic-convergence \
  ../rtmb_ebswp_form2 \
  cd46353
cd ../rtmb_ebswp_form2
```

The tests were run in that worktree on branch
`experiment/double-logistic-convergence`. Scenario-specific files were written
under `analysis/output/double_logistic_experiments/`, leaving the published
comparison objects unchanged. Each fit was restarted automatically and its
starting rule, prior scales, seed, objective, gradient, bounds check, and
Hessian check were retained.

#### Step 2: reproduce the original result

The unchanged configuration was reproduced with the dedicated experiment
runner:

```bash
POLLOCK_ROOT=/path/to/pollock \
  Rscript R/run_double_logistic_experiments.R
```

The reproduction matched the saved objective (8299.1812) and maximum gradient
(1.8366), including the `false convergence (8)` message. The objective and
independently evaluated report differed by less than $4\times10^{-12}$.
Restarting did not resolve the gradient, confirming the original result rather
than an input or reporting mismatch.

#### Step 3: improve starting values

The two-stage test was implemented as follows:

1. Fit one common double-logistic triplet to all years.
2. Replicate that fitted triplet across the 61 years.
3. Use the resulting matrix as the starting point for the annual option-2 fit.
4. Restart the annual fit from its solution and check whether the gradient
   decreases further.

This preliminary equality-mapped curve converged with objective 9101.7 and
maximum gradient 0.0005. Because its prior contribution was repeated for every
year, it was useful as a starting-value diagnostic but was not the intended
three-parameter model. The corrected shared-parameter fit is reported in step
6. When the preliminary triplet was expanded across years, the annual fit
returned objective 8299.0, maximum gradient 1.7937, and false convergence.
Better initialization
therefore helped only slightly and identifies the annual parameterization—not
the common double-logistic shape—as the main difficulty.

#### Step 4: test modestly informative regularization

After establishing the improved-start baseline, replace the original scales
with the proposed moderately stronger values

$$
\sigma_p = (0.50, 0.50, 0.35), \qquad
\sigma_\Delta = (0.25, 0.25, 0.20).
$$

The first set controls shrinkage of annual log parameters toward the central
double-logistic shape; the second controls year-to-year changes. The proposed
scales produced objective 8383.5 and maximum gradient 14.5524. Scale
multipliers of 0.75, 1.25, and 1.50 also failed, with maximum gradients of
15.0113, 2.7645, and 4.9645, respectively. The proposed stronger regularization
did not achieve estimability.

#### Step 5: use multiple starting points

For both the original and proposed regularization, 10 reproducible starts were
generated by applying small log-scale perturbations to the common-curve
solution. All results, including failures, were retained. Under the original
scales, objectives ranged from 8298.0 to 8299.5 and gradients from 1.8158 to
12.8581. Under the proposed scales, objectives ranged from 8383.3 to 8383.7 and
gradients from 6.6320 to 14.6955. All 20 fits returned false convergence. The
variation among endpoints, together with persistent large gradients, is
consistent with weak identification and local irregularity rather than a
single poor starting point.

#### Step 6: consider a hierarchical RTMB formulation

The intended model is not the original annual matrix treated directly as 183
random effects. It is a two-stage hierarchical parameterization:

1. Estimate one log-scale triplet $\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)$ shared by all
   fishery years.
2. Starting from that estimate, define each annual triplet as
   $\theta_t=\mu+\delta_t$.
3. Treat the annual deviations $\delta_t$ as zero-centered random effects.
4. Fix their log-scale standard deviation to
   $\sqrt{\log(1+0.20^2)}=0.1980$, corresponding to a 20% lognormal CV.
5. Integrate the annual deviations with the RTMB Laplace approximation while
   continuing to estimate the shared mean triplet and the other assessment
   parameters.

The stage-1 estimates on the natural scale were $p_1=1.6495$, $p_2=3.2743$,
and $p_3=9.4255$. That fit terminated with optimizer code 0 and maximum
gradient 0.00072. In stage 2, the estimated mean parameters shifted to
$p_1=1.4926$, $p_2=3.2328$, and $p_3=11.4924$. The marginal fit also
terminated with code 0 and maximum gradient 0.00027.

The fitted annual modes had across-year standard deviations of 0.2456, 0.2089,
and 0.1737 on the log scale for $p_1$, $p_2$, and $p_3$, respectively.
These correspond to realized across-year CVs of approximately 24.9%, 21.1%, and
17.5%. They need not equal the 20% distributional CV because they are conditional
modes informed jointly by the data and the random-effect distribution.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-form2-cv05
#| tbl-cap: "Corrected two-stage option-2 fit. The stage-2 objective is the Laplace-approximated marginal objective and is not directly comparable with the stage-1 joint objective."
#| echo: false

readr::read_csv(
  rtmb_file("reporting", "data", "double_logistic_cv05_summary.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  transmute(
    Stage = c("Shared three-parameter curve", "20% CV annual random effects"),
    Objective = round(objective, 1),
    `Objective type` = c("Joint", "Laplace marginal"),
    `Optimizer code` = convergence,
    `Maximum gradient` = round(max_gradient, 5),
    `Positive Hessian` = hessian_ok,
    `Finite standard errors` = finite_se,
    `Elapsed seconds` = round(seconds, 1)
  ) |>
  gt_report()
```

#### Section-2.6 formulation without the age-11-and-older equality

The preferred option-2 experiment now follows the three-parameter function on
the [selectivity prior-elicitation page](https://jimianelli.github.io/selex/):
the product of the ascending and descending limbs is smoothly capped near one,
ages 11--15 are not forced to share the age-11 value, and the associated
nonsmooth old-age shape penalty is omitted.

Both stages returned optimizer code 0. The shared-curve stage had a maximum
gradient of 0.00045 and the 20% CV random-effects stage had a maximum gradient
of 0.000068. The stage-2 evaluated total was 8173.4 and its fishery
age-composition contribution was 498.8.

The process-CV ladder started from the previously accepted 5% fit and increased
the allowance through 7.5%, 10%, 12.5%, 15%, and 20%. Every rung returned
optimizer code 0, a maximum gradient below 0.0001, a positive Hessian, and finite
standard errors. At 20%, the mean across-age temporal standard deviation of
selectivity was 0.239, compared with 0.068 at 5%; the largest age-specific
temporal standard deviation increased from 0.198 to 0.548. Fishery
age-composition NLL declined from 790.3 at 5% to 498.8 at 20%. The gains persist
through 20%, although the OSA diagnostics show that the double-logistic family
still leaves more aggregate structure than the base and 2D AR1 forms.

This is time-and-age variation through a parsimonious curve rather than a free
year-by-age surface: the three annual parameters move the ascending limb, peak,
and descending limb, thereby changing selectivity across ages each year. There
is no additional independent random effect for every age; that more flexible
structure is represented by the 2D AR1 alternative.

The stage-2 mean parameters were $p_1=1.41$, $p_2=2.94$, and $p_3=6.16$.
Selectivity declined smoothly after age 11; in 2024 its values at ages 11--15
were 1.135, 0.907, 0.689, 0.499, and 0.348 after within-year centering.

The earlier zero-eigenvalue warning was not created by these three selectivity
parameters. Two unused temperature-residual parameters, `resid_temp_x1` and
`resid_temp_x2`, had inadvertently remained in the experimental parameter
vector even though neither appears in the objective. Perturbing either from
-10 to +10 changed the objective by exactly zero. The 623-parameter Hessian
therefore had two numerical-zero eigenvalues and no substantively negative
eigenvalues. After mapping those unused parameters out, the current
621-parameter stage-2 Hessian is positive definite: its minimum eigenvalue is
0.1349 and finite standard errors are obtained.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-form2-old-age-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Option-2 comparison. The current section-2.6 implementation uses a smooth approximation to the cap at one, does not impose the age-11-and-older equality, and maps two unused temperature-residual parameters out of the optimization. Earlier capped rows are retained only as historical context. Stage-2 objectives are Laplace marginal objectives and should be compared only with other stage-2 rows."
#| echo: false

readr::read_csv(
  rtmb_file("reporting", "data", "double_logistic_old_age_sensitivity.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    Configuration = if_else(old_age_cap, "Earlier ages-11+ formulation", "Smooth section-2.6 formulation"),
    Stage = if_else(stage == 1, "Shared curve", "Annual random effects")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Configuration, Stage,
    Objective = round(objective, 1),
    `Evaluated total` = round(evaluated_total, 1),
    `Fishery age NLL` = round(fishery_age_nll, 1),
    `Maximum gradient` = round(max_gradient, 5),
    `p1` = round(p1, 2), `p2` = round(p2, 2), `p3` = round(p3, 2),
    `Positive Hessian` = hessian_ok,
    `Finite standard errors` = finite_se
  ) |>
  gt_report()
```

The earlier smallest Hessian eigenvalues, about $-1.2\times10^{-16}$ and
$-1.9\times10^{-16}$, were numerical zeros rather than meaningful negative
curvature. They corresponded to the unused `resid_temp_x1` and
`resid_temp_x2` parameters. Once those were mapped out, the current stage-2
minimum eigenvalue was 0.1349 and all standard errors were finite.

#### Step 7: decide whether a fit is usable

Each experiment should pass all of the following checks before its assessment
results are compared:

- optimizer convergence code 0;
- maximum absolute gradient below 0.001, with 0.0001 preferred;
- no important parameters at or very near their bounds;
- positive-definite Hessian and finite standard errors;
- objective value matching the independently evaluated reported total;
- stable results when optimization is restarted from the fitted values;
- similar solutions across reasonable starting points;
- smooth, biologically plausible annual parameter paths and selectivity curves;
- understandable changes in likelihood components, age-composition residuals,
  spawning biomass, recruitment, and fishing mortality; and
- conclusions that remain similar across modest changes in prior strength.

The lower objective value is only one diagnostic. Convergence, stability,
biological plausibility, fit to the observed compositions, and effects on
assessment quantities should be considered together.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-form2-experiments
#| tbl-cap: "Selected option-2 convergence experiments. Objective is the minimized total negative log likelihood; max gradient is the largest absolute element of the objective gradient; a positive Hessian is required for a locally stable solution."
#| echo: false

form2_experiments <- readr::read_csv(
  rtmb_file("reporting", "data", "double_logistic_experiment_summary.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

form2_experiments |>
  filter(scenario %in% c(
    "original_reproduction", "pooled_original", "common_start_original",
    "proposed_prior", "prior_multiplier_0p75", "prior_multiplier_1p25",
    "prior_multiplier_1p50"
  )) |>
  transmute(
    Scenario = recode(
      scenario,
      original_reproduction = "Original reproduction",
      pooled_original = "Pooled three-parameter fit",
      common_start_original = "Annual fit from pooled start",
      proposed_prior = "Proposed stronger prior",
      prior_multiplier_0p75 = "Proposed scales × 0.75",
      prior_multiplier_1p25 = "Proposed scales × 1.25",
      prior_multiplier_1p50 = "Proposed scales × 1.50"
    ),
    Objective = round(objective, 1),
    `Optimizer code` = convergence,
    `Max gradient` = round(max_gradient, 4),
    `At bounds` = at_bound,
    `Positive Hessian` = hessian_ok
  ) |>
  gt_report()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-form2-multistart-gradients
#| fig-cap: "Maximum absolute gradients from 10 perturbed starts under each regularization. The dashed line marks the 0.001 acceptance threshold; every annual fit remained well above it."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| echo: false

form2_experiments |>
  filter(grepl("^multistart_", scenario)) |>
  mutate(
    Regularization = if_else(
      grepl("original", scenario), "Original scales", "Proposed stronger scales"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(seed, max_gradient, color = Regularization)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.001, linetype = 2, color = "grey45") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "Starting-point seed", y = "Maximum absolute gradient", color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

| Stage | Configuration | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original fit | Original starts and scales | Completed | Code 1; gradient 1.8366; objective 8299.2; not usable for interpretation |
| Reproduction and restart | Unchanged model, then restart from saved solution | Completed | Reproduced false convergence; restart did not improve it |
| Common-curve initialization | Pooled triplet followed by annual fit | Completed | Pooled fit passed the gradient criterion; annual fit failed |
| Modestly informative scales | $\sigma_p=(0.50,0.50,0.35)$, $\sigma_\Delta=(0.25,0.25,0.20)$ | Completed | False convergence; gradient 14.5524 |
| Prior sensitivity | Scale multipliers 0.75, 1.25, and 1.50 | Completed | All three failed convergence and Hessian checks |
| Multiple starts | 10 original-prior and 10 proposed-prior perturbations | Completed | All 20 returned false convergence |
| Preliminary random-effects sensitivity | Existing absolute annual matrix integrated directly | Completed | Failed in RTMB's inner Newton optimization; this was not the intended hierarchy |
| Corrected stage 1 | Smooth section-2.6 curve shared across all years | Completed | Code 0; gradient 0.00045; positive Hessian |
| Corrected stage 2 | Smooth section-2.6 mean triplet plus annual random deviations with 20% CV | Completed | Code 0; marginal gradient 0.000068 |
| Uncertainty check | Hessian and standard errors after mapping unused parameters out | Completed | Minimum eigenvalue 0.1349; finite standard errors obtained |

Taken together, the tests reject the 183-parameter annual fixed-effect version
but support continued evaluation of the smooth section-2.6 20% CV
random-effects model. The next step is to compare its residuals and assessment
trajectories with the base and 2D AR1 alternatives.

::: {.callout-note title="Double-logistic estimability"}
The failed run described above estimated 183 unrelated annual fixed effects.
It has been superseded by the two-stage hierarchical fit shown here. In the
accepted Stage 2 configuration, the annual deviations are random effects with
a fixed 20% process CV around the shared three-parameter mean curve. This fit
passed the optimizer, gradient, Hessian, and finite-standard-error checks.
:::

## Form 5: 2D AR1 time-varying surface

The 2D AR1 form estimates a full year-by-age latent field $z_{t,a}$. Before centering, the log selectivity is

$$
\ell_{t,a} = z_{t,a},
$$

with the same age-11 plus-group constraint and within-year centering used for the other forms. The latent field is penalized with a separable AR1 process over year and age:

$$
z \sim \operatorname{AR1}_{\mathrm{year}}(\rho_y)
\otimes
\operatorname{AR1}_{\mathrm{age}}(\rho_a),
$$

with fitted correlations reported in the caption for @fig-sel-ridges. The scenario recipe down-weights the AR1 penalty relative to the default, allowing more interannual variation while still borrowing strength across neighboring years and ages.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sel-ridges
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Fishery selectivity through time (ggridges), normalized within year. The time-age varying double logistic is the stage-2 fit: annual random deviations around a shared mean curve with 20% process CV, a differentiable cap near one, and no age-11-and-older equality. Stage 1 was used only to initialize this fit and is not displayed. The stage-2 fit passed the optimizer, gradient, positive-Hessian, and finite-standard-error checks.", rho_ar1_caption)'
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10
#| out-width: "100%"

ridge_runs <- list(
  "Base coefficients" = runs[[which(forms == 0L)]],
  "Time-age varying double logistic (20% CV)" =
    runs[[which(forms == 2L)]],
  "2D AR1" = runs[[which(forms == 5L)]]
)

ridge_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(ridge_runs, function(run, approach) {
  sel <- run$report$sel_fsh
  stopifnot(is.matrix(sel), !is.null(rownames(sel)))
  out <- as_tibble(sel, .name_repair = "minimal")
  names(out) <- seq_len(ncol(sel))
  out |>
    mutate(year = as.integer(rownames(sel)), .before = 1) |>
    pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "age", values_to = "selectivity") |>
    mutate(age = as.integer(age), approach = approach)
}) |>
  group_by(approach, year) |>
  mutate(relative = selectivity / max(selectivity, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    approach = factor(approach, levels = names(ridge_runs)),
    year_factor = factor(year, levels = rev(sort(unique(year))))
  )

ggplot(ridge_df, aes(x = age, y = year_factor, height = relative, group = year_factor)) +
  geom_density_ridges(stat = "identity", fill = "#1f78b4", alpha = 0.65, rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  facet_wrap(~approach, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Year") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

# Spawning Biomass Comparison

```{r}
#| label: fig-ssb
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass (SSB) trajectories by fishery selectivity form."

ggplot(ssb_df, aes(x = year, y = SSB, color = label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "SSB", color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ssb-differences
#| tbl-cap: "SSB differences relative to base run at key years."

key_years <- sort(unique(ssb_df$year))
key_years <- key_years[key_years %in% c(max(key_years), max(key_years) - 1, 2000, 2010, 2020)]
if (length(key_years) == 0) key_years <- tail(sort(unique(ssb_df$year)), 5)

ssb_wide <- ssb_df |>
  filter(year %in% key_years) |>
  select(fishery_sel_form, label, year, SSB) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = fishery_sel_form, values_from = SSB, names_prefix = "form_")

base_col <- paste0("form_", base_form)

ssb_delta <- ssb_df |>
  filter(year %in% key_years) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    base_SSB = SSB[fishery_sel_form == base_form][1],
    delta_SSB = SSB - base_SSB,
    pct_delta = 100 * delta_SSB / base_SSB
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(label, fishery_sel_form, year, SSB, delta_SSB, pct_delta) |>
  arrange(year, fishery_sel_form)

ssb_delta |>
  mutate(across(c(SSB, delta_SSB, pct_delta), ~round(.x, 4))) |>
  gt_report() |>
  tab_header(title = "SSB deltas vs base")
```


# Appendix: Implementation References {#sec-appendix-implementation}

The equations above are implemented through the RTMB parameter builder, the selectivity construction helper, and the model likelihood. These references provide traceability without repeating the methods section.

## Parameter blocks

Fishery selectivity parameters are initialized in `R/utils-rtmb.R::add_fishery_selectivity_parameters()`. The defaults to check first are in `R/utils-rtmb.R:223-235`:

```r
add_fishery_selectivity_parameters <- function(parameters, data) {
  nyrs <- as.integer(data$endyr - data$styr + 1L)
  nages <- as.integer(data$nages)
  defaults <- list(
    sel_double_logistic_fsh = matrix(log(c(1.5, 3, 4)), nrow = nyrs, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE),
    sel_tv_ar1_fsh = matrix(0, nrow = nyrs, ncol = nages),
    sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh = c(0, 0),
    log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh = log(0.2)
  )
}
```

`R/Rpm.R:9-22` contains matching safety defaults. These matter when older saved parameter lists are evaluated without the newer optional selectivity blocks:

```r
if (!exists("fishery_sel_form", inherits = FALSE)) fishery_sel_form <- 0L
if (!exists("sel_double_logistic_fsh", inherits = FALSE)) {
  sel_double_logistic_fsh <- matrix(log(c(1.5, 3, 4)), nrow = endyr - styr + 1, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
}
if (!exists("sel_tv_ar1_fsh", inherits = FALSE)) sel_tv_ar1_fsh <- matrix(0, nrow = endyr - styr + 1, ncol = nages)
if (!exists("sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh", inherits = FALSE)) sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh <- c(0, 0)
if (!exists("log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh", inherits = FALSE)) log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh <- log(0.2)
if (!exists("sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh", inherits = FALSE)) sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh <- 1.0
```

## Selectivity construction

The base coefficient form is built in `R/model_funs.R:20-61`. The initial coefficients are centered, change-year deviations are applied, and selectivity is carried forward in years without a change:

```r
log_sel[1, 1:nsel] <- coffs
log_sel[1, (nsel + 1):nages] <- coffs[nsel]
log_sel[1, ] <- log_sel[1, ] - log(mean(exp(log_sel[1, ])))

if (ii <= nch_fsh && year == yrs_ch_fsh[ii]) {
  log_sel[i + 1, 1:nsel] <- log_sel[i, 1:nsel] + sel_devs[ii, ]
  log_sel[i + 1, (nsel + 1):nages] <- log_sel[i + 1, nsel]
} else {
  log_sel[i + 1, ] <- log_sel[i, ]
}
```

`R/model_funs.R:68-86` applies the age-11 plus-group constraint. This is the code that makes ages 11 and older share the same fishery selectivity value:

```r
if (ncol(log_sel) >= first_old_age) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(log_sel))) {
    log_sel[i, first_old_age:ncol(log_sel)] <- log_sel[i, first_old_age]
    if (isTRUE(center)) log_sel[i, ] <- center_log_selectivity(log_sel[i, ])
  }
}
```

`R/model_funs.R:102-180` dispatches among selectivity forms and returns the year-by-age log selectivity matrix. The most relevant branches for this comparison are `R/model_funs.R:117-123` for form 0, `R/model_funs.R:136-153` for form 2, and `R/model_funs.R:172-180` for form 5:

```r
if (form == 0L) {
  out <- compute_selectivity_fsh(...)
  out$log_sel <- cap_old_age_log_selectivity(out$log_sel, first_old_age = 11L)
  return(out)
} else if (form == 2L) {
  p1 <- exp(par_i[1])
  p2 <- exp(par_i[2])
  p3 <- exp(par_i[3])
  gamma1 <- p1 + p2
  gamma2 <- 2 * p1 + p2 + p3
  asc <- 1 / (1 + exp(-log(19) * (age_vector - gamma1) / p1))
  desc <- 1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-log(19) * (age_vector - gamma2) / p3))
  base <- log(asc * desc * 0.95^(-2) + 1e-12)
  log_sel[i, ] <- center_log_selectivity(base - max(base))
} else if (form == 5L) {
  for (i in 1:nyrs) log_sel[i, ] <- center_log_selectivity(sel_tv_ar1_fsh[i, ])
}

log_sel <- cap_old_age_log_selectivity(log_sel, first_old_age = 11L)
```

`R/Rpm.R` then exponentiates the returned log selectivity and applies it inside the annual fishing mortality calculation:

```r
sel_fsh <- exp(log_sel_fsh)
F[i, ] <- Fmort[i] * sel_fsh[i, ]
```

Thus, all scenario differences shown in the comparison report enter through the same population-dynamics pathway after the selectivity surface has been constructed.

## Selectivity penalties

`R/Rpm.R:283-298` calls `R/model_funs.R::selectivity_like_fsh_forms()` after the age-composition likelihood and before survey selectivity penalties:

```r
pen_fsh <- selectivity_like_fsh_forms(
  fishery_sel_form = fishery_sel_form,
  log_sel_fsh = log_sel_fsh,
  sel_double_logistic_fsh = sel_double_logistic_fsh,
  sel_tv_ar1_fsh = sel_tv_ar1_fsh,
  sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh = sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh,
  log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh = log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh,
  sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh = sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh
)
```

For form 2, `R/model_funs.R:805-819` applies the prior on annual log-scale double-logistic parameters and the first-difference penalty:

```r
target <- log(c(1.5, 3, 4))
prior_scale <- c(0.75, 0.75, 0.45)
rw_scale <- c(0.60, 0.60, 0.40)
for (i in 1:nrow(sel_double_logistic_fsh)) {
  dev <- dev + sum(((sel_double_logistic_fsh[i, ] - target) / prior_scale)^2)
}
for (i in 2:nrow(sel_double_logistic_fsh)) {
  dev <- dev + sum(((sel_double_logistic_fsh[i, ] - sel_double_logistic_fsh[i - 1, ]) / rw_scale)^2) / 2
}
```

For form 5, `R/model_funs.R:827-841` transforms the AR1 correlations, applies the old-age constraint to the latent field used in the penalty, and evaluates the separable AR1-by-AR1 density:

```r
rho_y <- safe_logit_rho(sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh[1])
rho_a <- safe_logit_rho(sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh[2])
f_year <- function(x) dautoreg(x, phi = rho_y, log = TRUE)
f_age <- function(x) dautoreg(x, phi = rho_a, log = TRUE)
sel_tv_ar1_fsh_pen <- cap_old_age_log_selectivity(
  sel_tv_ar1_fsh,
  first_old_age = 11L,
  center = FALSE
)
dev <- dev - sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh * dseparable(f_year, f_age)(sel_tv_ar1_fsh_pen, scale = scale)
```

## Scenario driver

`R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R` defines the scenario fits and writes the saved objects used by this report. The key setup is in `R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R:41-85`, where the form flag is set, form-specific starts are provided, and the AR1 penalty weight is relaxed for form 5:

```r
data$fishery_sel_form <- form_id
parms <- e$add_fishery_selectivity_parameters(e$parms, data)

if (form_id == 2L) {
  parms$sel_double_logistic_fsh <- matrix(
    log(c(1.5, 3, 4)),
    nrow = nyrs,
    ncol = 3,
    byrow = TRUE
  )
}
if (form_id == 5L) {
  parms$log_sel_tv_ar1_sigma_fsh <- log(1.2)
  data$sel_tv_ar1_weight_fsh <- 0.25
  parms$sel_tv_ar1_rho_fsh <- c(0, 0)
  parms$sel_tv_ar1_fsh <- matrix(rnorm(nyrs * nages, sd = 0.05), nrow = nyrs, ncol = nages)
}
```

The optimizer setup is in `R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R:121-148`, and outputs are saved in `R/run_fishery_selectivity_forms.R:151-170`. The report reads those saved objects from `analysis/output/fishery_sel_forms/`, so the figures and tables reflect the fitted scenario objects rather than recomputing the model inside the document.
